== Biography ==
James was born on 2 September 1832 the son of [[Glasgow-1450|Peter Glasgow]] and [[Scott-41744|Agnes Scott]].<ref>
'''Birth or Baptism''':
"Church of Scotland: Old Parish Registers - Births and Baptisms", database, 
National Records of Scotland, 
([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 11 July 2026), 
James Glasgow born or baptised on 2 Sep 1832, son of Peter Glasgow & Agnes Scott, in Haddington, Haddingtonshire, Scotland; 
citing Parish Number 709, Ref 70/171, Frame 2288.
</ref><ref>
'''Baptism of son James Glasgow''':
"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, 
({{FamilySearch Record|XTY7-KVK}} : accessed 11 July 2026), 
Peter Glasgow's son James Glasgow baptism on 2 Sep 1832 in Haddington, Haddingtonshire, Scotland, United Kingdom; 
citing Digital film/folder number: 7; FHL microfilm: 1067849; Record number: 14010796.
</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1450]] is assessed at 97% (proved). James Glasgow’s held baptism citation explicitly identifies Peter Glasgow, with Agnes Scott in the paired-family account. The Haddington sibling sequence and surviving census household support the specific father rather than a surname-only match.

Confidence concerns this recorded child and the selected father as identified by the held family evidence; maternity and the father’s upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Inspect the original Haddington OPR entry and compare residence/occupation across the sibling baptisms.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-1456 Baptism of son James Glasgow: "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database,  ( : accessed 11 July 2026),  Peter Glasgow's son James Glasgow baptism on 2 Sep 1832 in Haddington, Haddingtonshire, Scotland, United Kingdom;  citing Digital film/folder number: 7; FHL microfilm: 1067849; Record number: 14010796.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
